segments.text: Ladies and gentlemen, raise a warm applause as I introduce to you our panelists this morning, Devendra Mahato and why we have three very different people who have led or who continue to lead three very different thoughts when it comes to Gen Z.

If you saw this one man who went on a hunger strike until and unless his demands and the students' demands was accepted, it was Devendra Mahatoji who was right there. I have Anish Gawande who is from NCP Sharad Pawar but also found himself on the stage of the Kokro Janata Party during the Janata Mantra protest.

Devendra Mahato represents the aspirations of Gen Z, the youth coming in from towns like Ranchi, Jharkhand, the angst of the youth. If he represents that, then somewhere down the line Anish Gawande represents the angst of the youth which is literal Gen Z from the cities and what they feel and what their demands are. In the midst of it, ladies and gentlemen, raise a warm applause. I have Mr. Pradeep Bhandari.

who is from the Bharatiya Janata Party and represents another thought which many in this country align with, which include the Gen Z. So thank you all three of you for coming on India Today and our Mumbai Conclave. Mahatoji, sabse pehle main aapse shuru karungi. Itni lambi ladaiya apne ladhi laga tha, ki itne saare cameras aajayenge, itne saare log jur jayenge aapse.
This is the first time we have seen this. This is the first time we have seen this.

The history of eighty-eight years and in that struggle, the original soul was that our language, culture, style, tradition, tradition will be created. Our youth will get an opportunity. But in the history of twenty-six years of Jharkhand,
We have to do something, we have to do something.

jo parthiyon ki parichon par jiska bhavish nirbhar hai, jiska aaj paper leak lagataar ho rahi hai aur hum log lagataar sanghars kar rahi hai piche chabish saalo se. Lekin humare aavaj ko sir par sir ranchiyon ke sarco par dava diya jata hai. Police ke laathiyon par kuchla jaata hai. Humesa kahi na kahi aaj mere upar kayi baar laathi charge hui hai police ka. Kahi FHR humare upar darj hain. Hum iss umar pe jail tak kabhi sakwar kar chuke hain.

But today the whole world has come to know, this is a gift from all of you press media friends. And the whole world, the whole country, the students of Jharkhand have shown that if the struggle is not peaceful,

The problem that we are facing, we don't just give speeches. We don't just talk on the media. We fight along with the students on the streets. We fight along with the students in Satyagraha. We destroy the land. And that sixteen-day hunger strike that I had, I had to give a statement to the High Court, I had to warn the government that nothing should happen to the Devendranaths.
If you want to do something, you have to do it. If you want to do something, you have to do it. If you want to do something, you have to do it.

different isi le bhi tha and Anish I'd like to bring you in and let's make it a little bit Hindi and English because everyone can understand on the panel sabko samaj mein aayega to dono bhaashaon mein baat karenge. Par Anish it started off… it's parked off from your protest. Inke saamne Jharkhand ki Sarkar Jhuki, jo maan lijiye India Alliance ki Sarkar hai, aapke saamne Sarkar Jhuki aur jo CJP ki hai. Chaliye Anish is not part of the CJP but was very much part of that protest.

You were on the stage and at that time the Education Minister, Dharmendra Pradhan, had to resign. Did you feel the support? From where did this support come? The support on Instagram, the screen time you used to see that someone is talking, how did it come down on the roads of Jantar Mantar? How did that anger come down? Why was there so much anger on the streets? And the kind of support you got which enabled you to get the resignation of the Education Minister.

See, first of all, I want to say that the journey of student unity is very old. In 2016, you must have seen that there was an Occupy JNU Admin Block protest in JNU Admin Block. In 2019, you saw protests in Jamia, in JNU, you saw protests against the CANRC, it was crushed.

In 2026, when the protest against Neet Paper League started in Jantar Mantar, everyone felt that this protest will also be crushed, the student unity will be crushed again. But as the days went on, you saw one very powerful thing. You saw for the first time young people in this country recognized that we will fight for each other and we will stay united.

And that protest kept on growing. Farmers' movement got involved in it. You had various different movements joining in. And that protest kept on growing. Its voice kept on growing. One thing completely changed. That was fear. The entire fear disappeared from there. So why is the youth angry today? Why is this student unity coming back as a wave? Because young people are tired, you know.

You've turned democracy into a circus and expected all of us to be performing monkeys. Aaj hume chahiye accountability. Woh neat paper leak mein hum kya maang rahe the? Why was the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan important? For accountability. We want accountability for the seventeen year old girl who was raped in a park in New Delhi by three people pretending to be police officers.

We want accountability for the Ghatkopar flyover which is intersecting with each other after it's thirty percent complete and is being rebuilt. We want accountability for the MPSC paper leaks in Maharashtra for which thousands of students are still sitting at Joshi Bridge. And when the time had come to ask these questions and when we were repeatedly being called anti-national, urban nakshal, rajak,
Then we said that we will sit here, the struggle will start from here and you will say that this is a government in which there will be no resignations, but we will show you too.

I want to ask you one question, Anisha. What started off or what looked like as a temporary protest wave in Jantar Mantar has now clearly emerged as a pressure group. Gen Z has emerged as a pressure group.

sitting on the cusp of a possible Jantar Mantar 2.0 because all the demands that you say now your next demand is the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner of this country and tomorrow CJP is taking out a massive protest in Jantar Mantar. A. What are you hoping to achieve tomorrow? It's fairly simple, right? I think in some ways

a mockery of democracy is currently underway. How can you have such serious allegations being raised about the integrity of India's electoral process and your three election commissioners not give a press conference? Why is Sambit Patra giving a press conference for the election commission? The theatre of the observed is playing out and so we'll play theatre out onto the streets.

Pradeep, would you want to come in on this because you know there is something that the youth of this country is telling or rather something very uncomfortable that the youth of this country is telling the political parties today and I'm not just saying it's the BJP, it's as much as the Congress, look at the Congress, it espoused to be the champion of the voice of youth that could not even win an election in a DUSU election, right?

So, the uncomfortable truth is and let's bolster it with data. C voter ne ek survey kiya tha usme se che jo Gen Z ke log the unhone ne das me se che sixty percent ne bola ki hum kisi political party ko nahi trust karte. Somewhere down the line, political parties, the traditional national political parties have failed to connect with Gen Z. Do you agree with what's…

So I completely disagree. Let me begin my argument by showing you a picture because this ultimately is a fight between two narratives. All of you must have seen Skyrook… Ultimately, two narratives ke beech ki ladhaiye political.
I have seen a lot of people in India who are not aware of the importance of education.

You must have seen a start-up by Skyroot. This start-up had no family in business, no politician's son in the start-up and the government opened the space policy and now it's a one billion dollar plus valuation start-up employing more than one thousand people. This is the story of the new India which a lot of individuals do not see and this is why repeatedly one mandate after the other

you see pro-incumbency happening in the country where there is a global anti-incumbency environment. Let me take it. I completely agree that anything to do with paper league cannot… has to be addressed for sure. But morality cannot be selective and those who preach morality cannot be selective. Politicians definitely can be selective because of their political compulsions.

But if we speak about LEAK, we formed a committee under Nandan Neelkani and the committee is examining how to ensure that the entire education reforms can take place. But please look at what is happening in different states. Jammu and Kashmir, where the state… education is a state subject,

Twenty-two thousand students have been affected because of junior engineering examination leak. We've not seen any protest out here. Himachal Pradesh, where a class twelfth English examination has… paper has leaked, ninety thousand students have affected, not a single voice. Jharkhand, my dear friend, raised his voice. More than four lakh students were affected, but those who claimed themselves to be cockroaches were never seen there and were selective in it.

So if you speak about the young in the country, it cannot be selective. It has to be in unison. The young wants more representation in education institutions. This is why the number of universities have doubled.

the number of institutions have doubled, the IIT enrollment has increased by 1.25 times in terms of employment. Government employment was 2 lakh at the time of UPA, it has increased to 12 lakh. Private employment, if you speak about it, 17 crore, it was 2.5 crore at the time of UPA. And if you look at the per capita income of the young, it has doubled in the last 12 years.

Just ten seconds of another… Anish spoke about how could you have the Chief Election Commissioner not doing a press conference and why did the BJP come into the picture? What was the genesis of the story, Preeti? The genesis of the story was there was a newspaper who released a story based on a source-based information, quoting two election commissioners whose public court was not available. Uske basis pe Rahul Gandhi ne kaha hai, is desh ka election system bik chuka hai.

I want to ask you, until 1993, there was only one election commissioner in this country. So, from 1947 to 1993, were all the elections in this country? Second, UPSC is a very credible constitutional body. The UPSC has not been selected with the Chief Justice of India in the panel.

Do you believe that the UPSC examinations which have been conducted since 1947 to now are not neutral, are not fair? There are multiple constitutional bodies where the Chief Justice of India is not part of the panel. In fact, in that also, May 2023 the case had gone to the court and the court had said that it is the duty of the parliament to form a law. So let us put facts on one point and also another point Priti.

Just right now, Supreme Court, you were in Punjab. You were doing an interview for Bhagwanth Maan in Punjab. If you look at the last one and a half years, in which the court has said that rigging was done, the court has said that candidates were not allowed to vote. In which the state government's own advocate admitted that Punjab, where the elections of fifty to fifty municipal boards were cancelled.
But Pradeep, on two accounts, all that you said, the defense that you made, whatever you just said about EC,
You are such a senior journalist, just tell me and educate me.

If let's say hypothetically the chief election commissioner ne unilaterally decision liye, you remember the interview of S. Y. Khureshi, what does the 324 articles say? That either the majority of the opinion can decide or it has to happen unanimously. So I'm just asking you when it is not practically possible. It's about a constitutional body called the election commission of India.

and neither I can pontificate on it and I shouldn't. It's a constitutional body and the onus lies on the EC and one can question and should question, why should the principal political party answer for the EC? But I just want to come back, you know, circle back to what we are speaking of and which is what is the vision of the youth of this country and I'd like you to hold, jo aapne sabse pehle Pradeep ji aapne wo ek chitra dikhaya tha
But is it the oversimplification of what the youth wants in this country?

Mahato ji, aapko isme se kya samajh me aata hai? Kyunki jo Constituency Mahato ji represent karte hain, aapne itne saare IIT ke baat ki, inhi ke state me, inhi ke protest me, jab log baithe huye the, bohot log engineer banke nikle hain, unke paas naukri nahi hain. Engineer karke baithe hain, IIT jo wahan par local institutes hain, wahan se nikle huye hain, par 10,000 ki naukri par hain. To agar aap is binary me pad jaye hain, ki anarchist versus

you know, main narrative, it doesn't limit the demand, the angst of the youth. That's why my question was, that the principal parties… and Pradeepji, I am not talking about you, I am talking about Congress, I am talking about their party, the NCP as well, that they are not able to understand the language of the youth. Mahatoji, what he has shown that see, we are globally number one, this is just…
So, we have to do something about it.

The youths of today's young India, what do they want? This has to be understood first. These things… These political parties are understanding. BJP, Congress, GMM, they are understanding what youths of today want. I am trying to explain that how much they understand these things. You can understand that what does the youth of today want? The youth of today wants
economic freedom or economic security.

I can also rattle off statistics, a 30% increase in crime against women from 2014 to 2024.

Crimes against children have doubled from 2014 to 2024. Maharashtra is number one in crimes against children and number two in crimes against women. Every day, 36 women are sexually assaulted in the national capital. It's gone up from the time when we were at a moment in Nirbhaya where all of us were out onto the streets. There's a four lakh crore FIA outflow this year, which is more than you've seen in most years. Your net FIA outflows are almost negative. There's a 25.4% youth unemployment rate.

Graduate youth unemployment, as Matu Ji has said, is higher than those who don't have degrees. And if you pretend, ki sab changa si, then that is the problem. Even with the election commission, I have one very simple answer, right? You must restore public trust. I am saying that regardless of which party is in power, and this is something the NCPSP has maintained throughout the sort of course of history, right? Regardless of what party is in power, we must engage in dialogue, engage in discussion.

If the Bharatiya Janata Party is serious about restoring… If the Bharatiya Janata Party is truly serious about restoring faith in the election commission, please replace Gyanesh Kumar with Tukara Munde. That's it. Do it. Restore faith. Why are you not doing it? Does anybody… How many people here have faith in Gyanesh Kumar?

Complete one hundred percent faith. Elections must not only be free and fair, as the Lord Justice Hubert said about justice, they must be seen to be explicitly and unambiguously free and fair. And when questions are raised on that, we raise those questions as citizens of India. So what does, if you have, like I said, if from the perspective where you stand, one needs to rewrite the next five years of governance, what does it look like?
It means a restoration of competence. It means a restoration of accountability. And it also means an ability to say we were wrong. I am happy to say that the UPA did things that I disagree with.

I would really like to hope that after twelve years of BJP government, perhaps, just perhaps they can admit that some of the things that they did were foolish, instead of trying to paint demonetization as a master stroke, which we all will just laugh at at this point. Alright, so what basically he is saying, Anish and Mahatoji is also saying Pradeep and because your political party that you represent is actually holding the pen.

to write the next couple of years at least till 2029 and we can talk ahead. But you know there's a word that Gen Z uses which is gaslighting. When the Gen Z voted in Delhi University Student Union elections, Congress and the others got lesser vote than Nota. When the Gen Z voted in Punjab, Chandigarh University elections, Congress party and others did not get vote. When the Gen Z voted in Kerala, it was SFI and Congress was not even chosen. So the Gen Z continuously expressed their opinion through the ballot and the voting percentage of the young irrespective of whatever people say out here has consequently gone up, which reflects the public trust it has in constitutional body.

A silent minority which is political in nature cannot decide the fate of the we the people of India because we the people of India define the fate of the country, point number one. Point number two and a very factual point, I'll tell you what is gaslighting because facts always tell you the reality. This is 2013, August 2013, Bloomberg and I quote, the economic crisis in India, India is suffering the biggest economic crisis, unquote, maximum unemployment rate in young. So, we have to do something about it. We have to do something about it.

who called engineers in this country criminal. It was Mr. Ravind Reddy who called criminal. I am not saying that, Subhashankasi. What I am saying, Priti, is that we are moving in the right direction. And this is not just what I am saying. Every global rating agency has said that. Now on the part of the youth, please note, it's the young who vote out there. Aliens ni aake vote kar rahe hain, young hi kar rahe hain vote aake. Aur young hi bat rahe hain, agar unko public trust nahi hota to voting percentage kam ho jaata. Those who do not believe in the Supreme Court of India are those who are anti-constitutional. Because those who claim themselves to be cockroaches say what? Court. The Supreme Court has lost all credibility and nothing can be decided in the court of law. Now please tell me a matter which is sub-judiced. It cannot be decided based on street mobilization. Yeh ek lakh ki bheer le hai, 10,000 ki liye hai, 500 ki liye hai, mai bhi liye hai. Court usse nindya nahi karta. Jab election commission ka matter court ke andar hai, to inko yaat ho lag raha hai inka case weak hai, yaat ho inko lag raha hai ki court koi intimidate karna cha rahe hain, yeh inko court pe bharosa nahi hai.

Because whenever he went to the court in Bombay, if you recall, Maharashtra Chunawe said, what did Bombay High Court say? They said, not a single piece of evidence. More than six lakh eighty thousand opposition BLAs have been there. Not a single complaint. Then went on EVM. Election Commission said, come, hack. Not a single political party came.

Please note, right to protest, Preeti, cannot be taken in a way… and just ten seconds, the vision for the youth. The vision for the youth is India top three economies, India a leader in every field, that is what will provide maximum opportunities to the young.
So, I think it's a very important thing that we have to do, that we have to do something about it.

that there is a section of the youth, now it might be fronted by the CJP, is demanding for the resignation of the CEC. Because Pradeep, you gave a very good example that when objections were raised about the manipulations of the EVMs, at that point of time, what did the EC do? It immediately held a press conference and put an EVM there and said, try and hack it. Not a single political party came.

That's the question which I think many are raising right now. The prerogative doesn't lie on a Pradeep Bhandari, the prerogative lies on the Election Commission of India instead of a one-way communication. Because when it comes to the constitutional body of our country, then you know, Cesar's wife needs to be above suspicion, even Cesar's neighbor needs to be above suspicion.
in this case. So that's I think…

The election… I just want to take one more… one comment. The election commission, Pradeep, is accountable to the constitution and there is something called constitutional morality. So, therefore… Therefore, they don't… the election commission owes no explanation to anyone but to the people of this country. Definitely leave the opposition aside. Not the opposition, but to come out, you know, and…
point by point rebut every point that you have made instead of a one-way communication. I would think that when a lot of questions will be laid to rest if that happens. Final comments.
I have to understand what young Indian youth want. They want quality education.

Aamir aur gareeb ke beech me ek quality education ke liye koi diwaar aarthik diwaar na khaada ho. Dusra ek transparency, recruitment system chahta hai, jaha par naukriya bke nahi, unke mehnat ka aadar ho, unke sapno ka sammaan mile.
This is what we have to do, this is what we have to do.

people who vociferously put their point of view forward, one understands why there is debate, why there is discourse and we are privileged to have these three very diverse voices on this platform because they don't just represent who they are, they represent all those that they are speaking for.
